title: Residuals and union scale for studio players
summary: He and the players earned residuals when the union was strong; Steve Gadd did three sessions a day.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: That’s great. Do you get residuals for stuff that gets played again or played during certain events?

I used to, yeah. When the union was strong in that realm and when synthesizers hadn’t taken over yet, yes. You’d get residuals for whatever the run was and if they re-used it you’d get residuals again. Yeah. And the players did too. That was a great source of income for players.
Yeah they would come in and do a 60-second spot and whatever, get a union wage for that?
Yeah they’d do three a day. Steve Gadd was doing double scale, three a day. I mean I think he had checks at the union he never bothered to pick up. Have you interviewed Steve at all?
